lines.text: In the hall stands a clock that has never once been late. Tick, tick, tick. Never faster, never slower.
Music has a clock inside it too
The beat always walks under the music, like a floor under a dance. The notes can run or wait. The beat just keeps going.
A true story from music history.

A man named Maelzel sold a little ticking machine to keep the beat: the metronome. A Dutchman named Winkel actually built it first, but Maelzel’s name went on the box. Beethoven was one of the first composers to write metronome numbers on his music.
The clock in the hall would have approved.
The beat is the clock inside the music. It never hurries.
